summary: CONSENT. Both of my turn-1 SHOULD-FIX items are landed, and landed correctly rather than nominally. SF1 asked that Decision clause 4 stop presenting a four-identifier Stage A advisory set as a single Codex advisory; clause 4 now names CLAUDE-G31-V5-ADV-1, CLAUDE-G31-V5-ADV-2 / CODEX-G31-V5-ADV-1, and CLAUDE-G31-V5-ADV-3, and all four identifiers travel as honesty work. They are genuinely one class independently found twice, both identifiers are preserved, and the disposition is accurate. SF2 asked for frozen v3 to be pinned; the table now pins it at 68cccfcd between v2 and v4, the digest reproduces, and the repair went further than the row I asked for by extending the remeasurement clause's unmoved set to frozen v2/v3/v4, which is the harm SF2's whyItMatters actually named. All eleven cited digests reproduce byte-exact, including the three measured-input rows new at turn 2. The turn-1 subject is unmoved at 0fdea9aa and 0444. The full turn-1-to-turn-2 diff is confined to the two accepted repairs plus turn-2 protocol bookkeeping; nothing else moved, and no new claim was smuggled in behind the repairs. Live state reproduces: required-now 28, owners 32 of 32, last gate row DR-G32, DR-G31 OPEN, DR-104 DECIDED-V1-NOT-INTEGRATED, file 08 carrying G31. The D-167-through-D-207 non-unwrite span is complete at 41 of 41 with D-168 present. One advisory carries forward unrepaired from turn 1; it was held at advisory then for reasons that still hold, and I do not escalate it on no new grounds.

advisories.detail: 'After D-167, G31 is live and required-now is 28.' Unchanged from turn 1. Both conjuncts are true of the present and the sentence does not literally say D-167 set the cardinality, so it is not a false statement, but a reader may take the cardinality as D-167's effect. It was not: D-167 recorded 27 and D-169 took it to 28 by adding G32, a distinction file 08 line 417 preserves by listing D-167 and D-169 as separate naming decisions. I hold this at advisory for the same three reasons I gave at turn 1, all of which still hold: it sits in the narrative section rather than in a pinned measurement or a decision clause; the entry's operative statement of the number at line 87 is a live remeasurement carrying no attribution at all and is exactly right; and no act is directed on the strength of the attribution. I do not escalate it to SHOULD-FIX merely because a turn passed without its repair. An advisory is by construction not a condition of consent, and escalating on no new grounds would convert my own turn-1 grading into a moving target. Repair if convenient, at turn 3 or never: 'After D-167, G31 is live; after D-169, required-now is 28.'
